goal: Splits Bitcoin Core into separate node, wallet, and GUI processes communicating over IPC
Lays the foundation for running components independently, improving crash isolation and flexibility
reviewability: Ready to review now, no rebase or CI blockers pending
Expect to review the stable capnp-wrapper commits since the branch has been force-pushed many times over years
agreement: Broad, long-standing concept support from many maintainers (laanwj, gmaxwell, jonasschnelli, dcousens, jamesob, hebasto, promag)
Nonblocking objection: preference for a different serialization protocol, treated as out of scope (dcousens, gmaxwell)
Unaddressed old concept NACK, apparently stale (electorr)
Verified via architectural discussion of parameter passing and async design (laanwj)

categories.name: ipc
why: P1 because it is the core deliverable of the multiprocess project tracked in issue #28722
Directly unblocks two dependent open PRs and every future IPC feature
Benefit felt by the whole project and future contributors building on process separation

categories.name: build
why: P3 because it adds real CI and CMake support but only for an opt-in feature not built by default
Matters mainly to contributors actively working on multiprocess builds

categories.name: docs
why: P4 because the documentation changes are small and incidental to the code change
Limited to a one-line update describing a new library's scope

categories.name: wallet
why: P3 because it makes wallet interface types serializable without changing wallet behavior
A necessary prerequisite for the wallet to run as its own process, unblocking #19460

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it lets bitcoin-cli use IPC as an alternative transport to HTTP RPC
No change to existing RPC semantics or compatibility, so benefit is narrow

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because it extends the test framework to exercise multiprocess builds
Also pins down a real callback-lifetime bug with a regression test
Support work rather than new coverage of high-risk consensus or mempool areas

categories.name: tools
why: P4 because it is a purely mechanical devtools linter path update
No independent value beyond tracking the renamed interface boundary

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it fixes a real hang caused by a disconnected callback staying alive
Also fixes concrete build failures on macOS, FreeBSD, and MSan/TSan CI
Benefit felt broadly by anyone building or running the affected platforms
